utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to you, sir. We trust are you feeling a little better. Sorry that you've had to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... As we've dealt with other people in between. I would remind you, as it's a while ago, that the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, you were in the course of your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Memedi. I hope you are feeling better and if you need a break at any stage, don't hesitate to ask me or the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply an indication to start with, we discussed yesterday with our colleagues from the Prosecution in relation to the other witness whose evidence was interrupted last week, and we've gotten an indication that the witness would be called back for the remainder of that cross-examination. With that in mind, we have tried to shorten the end of the cross-examination of this witness to the extent that they are overlapping in part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, you will recall that when we left off last week I had showed you an indictment which had been signed by the public prosecutor Vlado Georgievski and we charged with you the crime of terrorism. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document this morning. It is P50 with an ERN ET-N002-0230-1. And the Macedonian version of that document is N002-0084-147. Sir, if I may ask you to look at the top of that document once it an appears in front of you. You will see that it comes from the criminal court of the Lower Court, Skopje II, Skopje. Can you see that? It's the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the first line should read: "The criminal court of the Lower Court, Skopje II, Skopje comprised of deputy president of the court, Verica Simovska, as presiding judge, and then it lists a number of judges. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see some sentences more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, perhaps I will give Mr. Memedi a paper copy, which may assist. And then in the same paragraph, sir, it refers to a number of accused person, and your name appears. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then at the end of the paragraph there's the date of the document, the 11 September and it says that it is a ruling, is that correct, or a decision?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... You to look at the next paragraph. It says what the rule something all about. It say it is -- custody is extended for the accused and then there's a number of accused person, and your name appear in that list. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it refers to a ruling of the investigative judge of the Lower Court Skopje II, Skopje with a number 438-01 of 14 August 2001 and a ruling with a number 439-01 of 14 August 2001. There's a ruling of a juvenile judge, and the decision is one of extension of detention for 30 days from 11 September 2001 to 11 October 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then underneath that paragraph, sir, there is what is translated in English as "statement of reasons." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I may ask the registry to turn to the second page of this document, both in the English and Macedonian version. Sir, I'll draw your attention to the second paragraph in the English with starts with the word, "Upon receipt of the indictment from OJO Skopje, KO number 2801-01 of 7 September 2001, the Trial Chamber of the court, ruling in accordance with its official responsibility, on the basis of Article 257, paragraph 2, examined whether or not the legal grounds still existed by which custody measures are set against the accused as considered in Article 184, paragraph 1, items 1 and 3 of the ZKPD, criminal procedure code." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the court said this: "In this particular instance there still exists legal grounds to extend custody against the accused provided for in Article 184, paragraph 2, items 1, 2, and 3, of the ZKP. This view of the Trial Chamber is reached on the basis of circumstances relating to the character of all the accused, who are young people, some with established families, and some without established families. The majority of the accused have no prior convictions and also the circumstances related to the crime for which there exists reasonable grounds for suspicion that the accused committed it, the severity, the manner of execution and the sentence envisaged for this criminal activity, the Trial Chamber finds that there is reasonable grounds for belief that there is a risk that were the accused released pending trial, they would flee in order to avoid criminal responsibility, or they would repeat the criminal activity." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph the Court said that on account of the above, the custody of all accused would be extended. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a prolonged detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Is that correct that the next paragraph -- the last paragraph in that document decides in effect to prolong your custody by 30 days?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says -- there is a signature by the deputy head of the court, is that correct, someone called Verica Simovska?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a note under the signature which suggests that an appeal against this ruling is allowed within three days after submission through this court directed to the appeals court in Skopje. Is that correct, that there is such a note in the document?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct also that you didn't use that opportunity to appeal against this decision?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this decision of the court was sent both to you and your lawyer, as is apparent from the list of persons to whom the decision was forwarded. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Weren't you represented by Niman Nimani at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any lawyer coming to my -- to prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Wasn't your first lawyer Mr. Tadir Fidovski and then Mr. Nimani?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this. But there was no lawyer coming to prison and to tell me that I'm your lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, also that there were three other decisions from that Court from the Trial Chamber of Skopje -- lower Skopje Court II in 9 October 2001, 9 November 2001, and 10 December 2001 where they prolonged your custody. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. Is that correct, sir, there were three other similar decision, three other similar rulings by the court to the effect that they prolonged your detention every time by a period of 30 days?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't go through those decisions because they are an available to Their Honours in the binder provided by the Prosecution. I will simply for the record read the ERN so that you may retrieve those decisions. The decision of 9 of October 2001 is P50, that's 5-0, with an ERN N002-0283-1. The decision of the 9 of November 2001 is again P50 with an ERN N002-0296-1. And the decision of the 10th of December 2001 is P50 with an ERN N002-0307-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, sir, that on all four occasions, on all four decisions there was the possibility given to you to appeal against the decision of detention?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And on none of those occasions did you appeal the decision. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you another document which is P50, with an ERN ET-N002-0285-1. Sir, if I may draw your attention to the top of that document when you receive it in the Macedonian. I have the ERN, I apologise. It is N002-0084-202. Sir, is this copy more legible in Macedonian or would you like a paper copy as well?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, we'll perhaps provide the more readable paper version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall that -- do you recall that on 24, 25th and 26th of October of 2001 there was a hearing in relation to your case where your lawyers challenged the jurisdiction of the court. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We will go through the document together then. If you can look at the top of that document, it's again coming from the Trial Chamber of the Lower Court, Skopje II, Skopje and it's again a ruling or a decision, depending on the translation. Can you see that? It's the first paragraph, sir. The very top of the first page and then there's a subheading saying ruling or decision, depending on the translation.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if can you still focus on the first paragraph it says in the middle of it that's it a ruling on the objection submitted for the accused by the defence counsels and then there's the name of the counsels. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it says -- there's another section, it says ruling and it says there is an objection submitted by the accused and it is the name and there's your name as well. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And this paragraph also says that the objection has been rejected as unfounded. Can you see that? That's the last few words of this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then underneath there is a statement of reasons and if I may ask the registry to turn to the next page both in the Macedonian and the English. In my translation, that may be one page further away. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're working on two different translation, but it seems that the content is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I would just like to draw your attention to a paragraph that starts either with the word "on 24 September 2001" or with the word "the accused Ali Isni and Ljatif Aliovski." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you go through that paragraph you will see that on 25th of October 2001 the lawyer of these two accused raised an issue concerning the paraffin glove tests which had been carried out on their clients -- on his clients, rather. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in particular the lawyer in question raised the possibility that the nitrate which had been found on the hands of one of the accused, Mr. Isni Ali, could be the result of a piece of shell which he said he touched or the result of agriculture products which were available at the time. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if I may ask to you go to the next page and that would be starting on the bottom of this page in the English but then moving on to the next page, please. There's a paragraph starting with the words "the accused Murtezan Murtezani, Sulejman Zendelovski" and so on. Can you find that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In the middle paragraph there is a passage which in my translation reads as follows: "Only the accused Farush Memedi exercised his right to remain silent and they were interrogated for the crime of terrorism pursuant to Rule 313 of the KZ, criminal code, to which the accused give clear and unambiguous testimony in which they completed denied the accusation." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then if we jump over one sentence there's another one says this -- that should be still be at page two of the Macedonian version, I believe. It is stated that, "In preparing the indictment the OGO Skopje has made additional error and formal mistakes, especially in the case of the accused Farush Memedi, who exercised his right to remain silent and the OJO Skopje accused him without consent of the investigating judge." Can you see that part?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The decision goes on to say: "The statement of the president of the Republic of Macedonia as well as the opinion of the government in connection with amnesty had also been placed before the Trial Chamber. It is stated as well that in the sense of Article 124, paragraph 1 and 2" --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I believe that would be the next page notice English, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "It is stated as well that in the sense of Article 124, paragraph 1 and 2 of the constitution of the Republic of Macedonia in the Republic of Macedonia, there was no declared state of war and the question is posed with whom an armed attack was taking place and in what enemy army the accused served. Finally, the question is posed on what sort of evidence is the indictment grounded, in view of the fact that the main proof is the paraffin glove tests which were taken on the accused who were in contaminated terrain where nitrate particles were present. It is proposed that the objection be sustained and the criminal proceeding stopped." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... To the next page, please. Sir, do you recall your lawyer making those objections for you?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can now look at the paragraph which should start: "The Trial Chamber, after review." In the other translation which you have on your screen that's the paragraph started "after the insight into the file." Do you see the last part of the sentence which referred to oral statements which have also been put forward verbally by the representative of the accused at the session held on 24, 25, and 26 October 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the Trial Chamber affirms that the objection is ungrounded and as such will be rejected. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then the court said this in particular: "In the particular instance of the objection the facts is contested that the accused carried out the crime attributed to them since the accusation is based on insufficiently confirmed facts and evidence and is based exclusively on the paraffin glove tests of the accused during which nitrate particles were found without any other evidence found against the accused." Can you see that part?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Explain this: "In this phase of the proceedings when the Trial Chamber is ruling on the objection to the indictment solely on the basis of the minutes obtained in the previous proceedings in accordance with Article 267 of the criminal procedure code, it cannot influence in advance the resolution of those questions which will be the subject of a hearing in the trial. In this sense the disputed matters fall within the jurisdiction of the Chamber, which will decide at the hearing where in the contradictory firsthand and verbal proceedings acquired on the basic principles of the criminal proceedings the fact and material truth can be directly confirmed." And then there's a signature again of the same deputy head of the court Verica Simovska. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's an indication that no appeal of this ruling is permitted and again the decision was forwarded to all of the accuseds and to their counsel. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to. I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you, sir, is that correct that the document was signed by the deputy head of the court, a person named Verica Simovksa and that there's an indication in this decision that there can be no appeal from the decision. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that also correct that at the end of the document, sir, there is a list of persons and one institution to whom this decision was forwarded. Can you see that list?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you see your name on it as well?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the name of a defence counsel called Tadir Fidovski?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply to apologise perhaps for the problems with the translation, but there appears to be several translation of the same document in several exhibits of the Prosecution and sometime no translation. We didn't realise before this moment that a different translation of the document would be shown on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, is that correct that you were never acquitted of these crimes with which you were charged but that you were eventually pardoned by the president of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not guilty of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But is that correct, sir, that you were never acquitted formally by the court but that were pardoned by the president?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were pardoned by the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And did that occur in the month of December 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened on the 14th of December, 2001, when I was pardoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, sir, that in the decision of pardon the president stated that you had been a member of a terrorist organisation, the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is P50 with an ERN ET-N002-0332-1, and the Macedonian version is again P50 N002-0084-249.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, if I can ask to you look at the top of that document. It starts with the words --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could perhaps just move up the English a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It starts with the words "an excerpt," and underneath, it says "On the decision of pardoning individuals, members of the so-called ONA or LNA deprived by liberty for acquittal of criminal prosecution." Can you see that? Sorry, sir, I'm not sure you have heard me. Can you see the top of that document where it says, "On the decision of pardoning individuals, members of the so-called ONA, deprived by liberty for acquittal of criminal prosecution. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree that it is signed by the president of the Republic of Macedonia, Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the first paragraph of that document it refers to an amnesty law and then it says that the president of the Republic of Macedonia on this case 18 December 2001 handed down a decision. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the decision says that it relates to the pardoning of individuals, members of the so-called ONS, this time, LNA deprived from liberty on their acquittal of criminal prosecution, and then it refers to one of your neighbours or villagers from Ljuboten, Mr. Ali Isni, saying that he's been discharged of criminal prosecution on the case of the Basic Court Skopje number 983-01. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct, sir, that you received a similar decision of amnesty signed by the president at the time?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A similar decision was issued but here it says Ali Xhavit Isni.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, but you received a similar decision in terms of content with your name on it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. I'm very grateful. I'm grateful for your patient, Mr. Memedi.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm finished with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mettraux. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Good morning, witness, Farush Memedi. My name is Antonio Apostolski and together with my colleague Jasmina Zivkovic I appear for Mr. Johan Tarculovski. Today I will ask you several questions related to the events in Ljuboten in the period between the 10th and the 12th of August, 2001. You stated that you lived in Ljuboten. You have completed secondary education in 1984. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In 1996, you served the conscription service in Stip. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me which was your military branch where you served?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Artillery, 120-millimetre mortar unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were trained in using infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that while you were serving in the army, you had received training in using infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean small weapons, light weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to light infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You are a member of the political party Democratic Union for Integration. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The abbreviation for the party is DUI, D-U-I. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: President of the party is Ali Ahmeti. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: He is now a MP in the Macedonian Assembly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: He was elected as a member of the parliament in the parliamentary elections in 2006. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Ali Ahmeti was an MP in the previous convention of the parliament of Macedonia which was elected in 2002. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 2001, Mr. Ali Ahmeti was the leader of the terrorist organisation ONA, NLA?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Gesim Ostreni is a distinguished member of DUI as well?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean if he is a member of the BDI.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that Gesim Ostreni is a distinguished member of DUI, DUI, of the Democratic Union for Integration?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me who is the president of the branch of DUI in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the village of Ljuboten there are many supporters of DUI?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, I don't know either, how many supporters there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that there are more than 100 DUI supporters in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe there are, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that NLA members became members of DUI after the conflict in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. Whoever wanted to become a member, he became one.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that before that, you were a member of the democratic party of the Albanians?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the abbreviation for the democratic party of the Albanians is DPA?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by DPA? The Albanian democratic party?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct -- yes, Democratic Party of the Albanians. The abbreviation is DPA in Macedonian, PDSH, S-H, in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Albanian it is PDSH.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that PDSH had members in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not showing that much interest in politics. I really don't understand your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Since you told me that you were a member of DUI and before that, you were a member of the PDSH party, my guess is that you are aware of the political developments. This is why I'm asking you. Is it correct that in 2001 PDSH had its members as members of parliament in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that PDSH had ministers in the government of the Macedonia in 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the MPs were elected in free and democratic elections in 1998?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you personally go and vote in the elections?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to 1998, those elections.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: No one forced you to turn out in the elections and vote, and nobody told you whom to vote for. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It's my own right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Right, thank you. On Friday, the 10th of August, 2001, at 8.00 in the morning, you heard shooting coming from the northern ridge above Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You saw shells falling as well as bullets onto the houses. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me how many shells you have seen falling in the village of Ljuboten on Friday, the 10th of August, 2001, at 8.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 8.00 in the morning when shooting was heard coming from the mountain above. This lasted for a while. Then shelling started and some shells fell in the vicinity of the mosque. Following this, we went into the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me how many shells fell?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not an expert in those matters, and I didn't count how many shells fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On the next day, the 11th of August, you heard only bursts of fire. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, sporadic fire.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that on Saturday, the 11th of August, no shells fell in the village of Ljuboten? There was fire coming only from light infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So if there would be anyone testifying before this Court that on Saturday, the 11th of August, 2001, shells fell in the village of Ljuboten, that would be incorrect?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was raining that day. There was lightening, and I really cannot say whether it was shelling or thunder.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On Sunday morning, on the 12th of August, 2001, around 8.00 in the morning, you heard shooting as well as shelling. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we -- as we were asleep, there was shooting. We were sleeping in the basement. I woke up and started to wonder what was going on, and then I went to the check-point and I no longer saw what happened in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that before 8.00 in the morning there was no shelling against the village of Ljuboten? I'm now referring to Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening. On Sunday evening, there was no shelling. But on Sunday morning, the shelling began.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that it started at 8.00 in the morning, the shelling, on the Sunday?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Around 12.00 you decided to go to Ljuboten following the Ljuboten road. Is that --

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, together with my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you were walking down the Ljuboten road, right before the check-point Buzalak 200 metres away, you stopped to get some rest. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you know in advance that there was a check-point at that location?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did your knowledge of the check-point being there constitute the reason why you decided to stop there and take some rest?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was very tired, and that's why I stopped there to rest. And this was far from the check-point. I would say about one kilometre far from the check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown, please, his statement, the number 26 -- Prosecutor's Exhibit 266, page 3 in the English version, and page 4 in the Macedonian version. Paragraph 11. Page 3 in the English version. And Macedonian version, it is page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In paragraph 11 of your statement that you see now -- do you see the paragraph 11 in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You state: "Before the Buzalak check-point, I decided to rest a bit with my family."

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: "I could see lots of people passing me, and after a while, we also continued to walk toward the check-point. Before we arrived to the check-point, a blue police jeep stopped and some policemen came out of the car, ordering us to form a line. At this stage, we were about 200 metres away from the check-point." That is contained in your statement. Is it correct that it was from that spot that the police took you and then they took you to the Butel police station?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Then, from the Butel police station, you were taken to the Prolece police station, where you were subjected to paraffin glove tests. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: There was a stop in my examination in chief, because I was going through my statement which is in evidence, and I believe that my learned colleague is doing exactly the same, asking him questions which are already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think you're right, Ms. Regue, but I -- I think the point is, Mr. Apostolski, you're putting a number of matters and simply saying is that right, and those matters are simply confirming the evidence that has already been given. It is just unnecessary repetition.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am aware of this being the case. I know it, but I think that these questions should take me to the question which I think is pertinent for me, so that I would not skip directly from one topic to another. My next question would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if you want the Chamber to be lenient to you in this matter, Mr. Apostolski, I'm sure the Defence will be more lenient of the Prosecution in the future. Even-handed. Carry on, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would deal with one more question only, since my colleague Guenal has cross-examined the witness in detail with regards to the paraffin glove test and also the course of the procedure before the Macedonian Court. You replied to my colleague Guenal that you were not aware that in the procedure before the Basic Court, the Lower Court, Skopje II you were represented by the attorney Niman Nimani.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 5, paragraph 23 of the English version of his statement that he has in front of him already. It will be page 7 in the Albanian text. Paragraph 23 where in line 7 of paragraph 23. So this would actually be in the following page of the Albanian version, 8th page of the Albanian version. Yes. Could you move the page towards the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You state that, "I think there was an Albanian lawyer who was supposed to represent us. As far as I remember, his name was Niman Nimani and he is a well-known lawyer in Macedonia." Is it correct that Mr. Niman Nimani has represented you in the procedure before the court?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a man in the court. As far as Niman Nimani is concerned, I don't know him. The man that was there, maybe he was a lawyer or I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You state that Niman Nimani was a well-known attorney in Macedonia. I think, then, that you must know him for to you say this.

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know this man. If I saw him today I wouldn't know him, but people say that Niman Nimani is well-known, while me personally, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I read just your statement, so that I don't have anymore questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have any more questions for this particular witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Regue

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Memedi. Mr. Memedi, my colleague for the Defence, just asked you whether Ali Ahmeti was a leader of a terrorist organisation, NLA in 2001. And you replied yes, sir. Did you believe in 2001 that NLA was a terrorist organisation?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Could we please bring up in e-court Exhibit P00050, pages 45 to 54. And then if we could go to the 5th page in the English version and the 4th in the Macedonian. The next page, sorry, of both documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Mr. Memedi, my colleague show you the other week this document. This is it an indictment from the Skopje court. And I'm going to read to you the paragraph which is just in the centre of the document. It says: "On 12 August 2001, between 8 hours and 12 hours in the village of Ljuboten, Skopje area, they," referring to you, "the accused, participated in an armed conflict as combatants against the Republic of Macedonia. In such a way, that during the intensive combating actions against the Armed Forces of the Republic of Macedonia located near the village with infantry fire-arms and ammunition, up until the moment when they were forced to withdraw, disposing of the weapons and the equipment they had while withdrawing and when attempting to leave the village headings for Skopje were met and detained." I'm going to stop there, Mr. Memedi. My question is: In the morning of 12 August 2001 between 8 and 12 hours were you involved in the activities that this document states, meaning you participate in an arm conflict against the forces of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Where were you during that time?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at home in the basement of my house, because there were shootings.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The last line of this paragraph reads: "You, the accused, had paraffin glove test made and presence of nitrate particles was determined with all accused and demeanour." Mr. Memedi, did you ever hold a weapon between the weekend 10 to 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Then also my learned colleague show you Exhibit P 00050, which was a decision pardoning Ali Isni, and you said that you had received the same document. In that document it said that Isni Ali, and I suppose you, were members of NLA, of the terrorist group. Mr. Memedi, have you ever been a member of a terrorist organisation?

utterances.speaker: FARUSH MEMEDI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be pleased to know, Mr. Memedi, that that concludes the questioning for you in those proceedings. We wish to thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance you have been able to give, and we're sorry that because of your illness your stay here was longer than expected. You may now, of course, return to your home and your ordinary affairs. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also thank you, all the bad I had inside me, I could express it. And I wish you a fruitful work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now go with the court officer, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Regue.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution is ready to call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it is it probably going to be more practical to have the break now and then commence with the witness after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If I may very briefly, there is a number of procedural matters which relate to witness which we indicated yesterday and perhaps with the leave of the Chamber we could do so after the break shortly before the witness comes, if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is not convenient to deal with them now?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I can do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Let's try now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The matter which we would wish to bring to the attention of the chamber concerns the two statements of Mr. Hutsch, who is going to appear now as a witness. The statements of Mr. Hutsch are filled with references to "sources" and to certain individuals who allegedly gave him information in relation to which he will now be asked to give evidence. The fact that Mr. Hutsch did not identify or name any of those sources or people obviously hampered the Defence ability to seek to verify those stories. As a result of that, we have exchanged a number of letters with the Prosecution with a view to ask the Prosecution to ask Mr. Hutsch to identify these persons. There was a first exchange of letter which related to two person who Mr. Hutsch claims accompanied him during visits to the village of Ljuboten. The Prosecution in turn asked Mr. Hutsch to disclose the names of these alleged people. Mr. Hutsch has continued to do so. There was another exchange of letters in relation to, I believe, 25 or so other paragraphs in the statements where Mr. Hutsch refers to alleged sources and alleged individuals, and again the Defence sent letters to the Prosecution asking them to ask Mr. Hutsch to identify those people or those sources, and I believe that but for one and perhaps two of those questions Mr. Hutsch has again refused to disclose the name of these alleged person or alleged sources. In its correspondence the Prosecution has at first indicated that the Prosecution would refuse to disclose this information based on the Rule 70 of the Rules of Procedure. The Prosecution later clarified that it was Mr. Hutsch who had requested Rule 70 procedure. We have also indicated in our letters to the Prosecution that we very serious issues as to the reliability and truthfulness of this witness, and Your Honour will be able to evaluate this matter in cross-examination. The result of this situation is that the Defence has not been able to investigate and verify a large number of matters which this witness will want to testify about. I would also like to bring to Your Honours' attention the fact that the exact same issue arose in the Milosevic case when Mr. Hutsch appeared as a witness for the Defence. And submissions were made at that time by the Prosecution in the following terms. It's the transcript of 12 October 2004 at page 32.898, and the person speaking is Mr. Geoffrey Nice. He says this: "My I while addressing you on this point in general terms say only this. I was given notice by Ms. Higgins half an hour ago that the issue might arise but very little, almost no details of how it would arise. If it is going to be suggested that this witness can say 'I was told by X the following but I'm not prepared to reveal who X is,' why, then, we will challenge that evidence as wholly inadmissible because, of course, it would have absolutely no truth value that the Court could attach to it, not knowing who X is and I not being in any sense or way allowed to cross-examine as to X is." The extent of the gaps, if I may call them that, in the evidence, the proposed evidence of this witness has created very serious concern for the Defence and the Defence may also, Your Honour, after having heard the evidence and after cross-examination, seek the exclusion of the entirety of the evidence of Mr. Hutsch, if he indeed declines to reveal these alleged sources and person to whom he says he talked or from whom he says he obtained information. And so that the Trial Chamber is fully briefed in this matter, Your Honour, and with the court's usher's assistant we have prepared what we believe to be the complete collection of letters which we have exchanged with the Prosecution. There's copies for the Court and a copy for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you amplify a little the course of this interesting exchange in the Milosevic case. Did it lead to any decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there were, as you will see during the cross-examination, a number of issues which are also relevant in relation to this case. However, Mr. Nice did not ask the witness to reveal any of those sources which he was concerned about so that the evidence was, in fact, omitted. There were a number of other procedural issues which were raised in the few previous pages of this transcript in relation to communication between Mr. Kay, who had called this witness, and the request of the witness in relation to his sources. Your Honour may find those references, but to answer Your Honour's question, there was no decision specifically relating to whether or not the evidence of Mr. Hutsch could be admitted. There was simply no objection raised at the end of the evidence by the Prosecution. There are two very quick matter which I would like to bring to Your Honours' attention in the sense of a forewarning. There is a number of documents which we had submitted to CLSS, in particular documents in German but also documents in the Macedonian language which related to the witness Mr. Hutsch, and unfortunately, we have not received yet the -- some of those translation. Others have been returned to us, CLSS having refused to translate those. So what we had to do in relation to these particular documents, we had to an official translations ourself both from the German language or from the Macedonian language, and those are the document which we will use with this witness and we will resubmit those documents so simply await the official translation of those documents which are still with CLSS. Finally there's an issue concerning still Mr. Hutsch and it relates to a number of documents pertaining to this witness which we have asked to obtain from a particular source. And that source has not yet responded to the request we are -- we understand that the source has identified a number of document which may be relevant and may be important to this particular witness and we understand that they've been working on it in the course of this week. We hope to receive this material before the end of this witness' evidence. And if indeed that is the case we will make all arrangement to translate, to read and review those document so that Mr. Hutsch does not have to be recalled for further evidence, but we simply wish do indicate to Your Honours that if these documents were not received on time and if indeed they were relevant and important, we may have to seek to re-call Mr. Hutsch for further cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Saxon, is there anything that you would submit?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The summary of the history of the issue of Mr. Hutsch's willingness to reveal his sources, his journalistic sources is generally accurate, the summary provided by Mr. Mettraux. It may be that - and this is my mistake - it may be that I may have used the term claiming Rule 70 protection perhaps too broadly in one of the letters, because I simply have to clarify that the Prosecution has not received the names of these sources from Mr. Hutsch. So this is not a situation, for example, under Rule 70 B where information is provided to the Prosecution but the source of the information refuses to grant permission for that information to be disseminated further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would have thought the Rule deals with information in the hands of the Prosecutor and this, from what we're told, is not. This is information in the hands of a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Absolutely. And the witness as a professional journalist is refusing to divulge the identities of his sources to anyone, because the witness is concerned about their security. That is the state of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And yet the Prosecution wants to rely upon that evidence. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On certain hearsay evidence, that would be a correct statement, Your Honour. On certain evidence that came from one of these sources, that would be a correct statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So the Prosecution asks the Chamber to except hearsay evidence from a source that is not disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then to rely upon that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. That is the Prosecution's position. The Prosecution believes that this should be a matter of weight that should be determined by the Chamber upon receipt of all the evidence not only from this witness but from other witnesses as well, and other sources. And if the Chamber prefers, the Prosecution is also in a position to lead from the witness with respect to the -- Mr. Hutsch's interpreters. Prosecution is prepared to present evidence demonstrating the reliability of the information provided through these interpreters which Mr. Hutsch then produced either in his notebooks or as part of his media articles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there anything further, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour, simply to make two points. The first one relates to the suggestion of journalistic sources. We would wish to bring to the attention of the Trial Chamber that this fact will have to be established, whether the sources were in fact used by Mr. Hutsch as a source for any journalistic work, which is the first matter. The second matter, Your Honour, is the proposal just made by my colleague Mr. Saxon in relation to the two interpreter. I would like to bring to the attention of the Chamber that we have actually asked the Prosecution to identify these individuals so that we could indeed talk to them and carry out an investigation in relation to some of the claims that Mr. Hutsch is making, and we received a response from the Prosecution to the effect that they did not have the information as to who those people are. So we are somewhat surprised by the suggestion made today, if that is indeed the suggestion, if I've understood it correctly, that the Prosecution knew -- know or knew who those people are. If that is the case, we would be very grateful to get an indication of their names so that they may be conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, once again, the Prosecution does not know the identities of these persons. That was not the proposal of the Prosecution a few minutes ago. The Prosecution's proposal was simply to demonstrate through the witness the reliability of his work as a journalist obtaining information through his interpreters. And that can be done, Your Honour, the Prosecution submits, without divulging the identities of these interpreters. If I may say so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have lost me completely, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, then let me start again. The witness is able to explain the system that he used to hire interpreters and the system that he used to work with interpreters to make sure that the information that he received while he was an investigative journalist in Macedonia was accurate. That is the point. And the witness can discuss this if that would be of assistance to the Trial Chamber. Secondly and finally, it seems to the Prosecution that there have been a number of cases where interpreters have -- that identities of interpreters have not been identified between the parties for their own security, and if the -- if this was a criteria for the admission of evidence in this Tribunal, then I believe there would have been a great deal of evidence in prior cases that would not have been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber understands from submissions that no particular order or decision is called for at this point. The Chamber will hear the evidence, including learning from the evidence whether the issues that have been debated are raised, and we will then deal with the consequences if they should arise in due course. Could I just note for the record that while I didn't specifically call upon Mr. Apostolski, I had a clear visual impression that this was an issue between Mr. Mettraux and the Defence of Mr. Boskoski and the Prosecution and you had no wish to participate. Did I judge it right, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence of Mr. Tarculovski fully supports the statements by my colleague Mr. Mettraux so that the Defence counsel of Mr. Tarculovski fully supports this stand by my colleague Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber will adjourn now and resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this time the Prosecution calls Franz-Josef Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hutsch, would you please take the card and read aloud the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, please sit down. Due to your physical configuration, you will actually be asked by the man immediately to your right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hutsch, perhaps before we begin, because we're both going to be speaking in English right now, I'd like to advise to you to please try to speak a little bit slowly and to pause after you hear my questions before you respond in order to give the interpreters a moment to catch up both with my words and your words, all right. First of all, for the record your name is Franz-Josef Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you are a citizen of Germany?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you serve in the German army?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When did you enter the Germany army?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: In October 1982.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you describe the progression of your career in the German army.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I first was trained as a reconnaissance Sergeant. After five years, I change career to become an officer. I did the normal officer's training in the German army, which contains technical analysis, technical planning, leadership. After that, I became a platoon leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you became a platoon leader what was your rank?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: First lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then after that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Then after that, I continued my career as a normal army officer. That means I became a member of the staff of a battalion. In that case that was S-2 section. That means intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then did you have experience, for example, with artillery and the use of artillery?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yeah. I was also trained as a forward observer for mortars and artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you just describe for the Chamber what the position or job of a forward observer is?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: A forward observer has to lead the fire of mortars and artillery to the target, wherever it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And what was your -- when did you leave the German army?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I left the army in April 1995 in the rank of a captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. When you left the army, the German army in 1995, did you start another career?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I became a journalist and by the situation in the Balkans, I became a war journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the first area of the Balkans that you worked in as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I entered Bosnia in May 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. If I can turn your attention to later in the 1990s, did there come a time when you decided to cover -- when I say cover, I'm speaking as a journalist, report about the events in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes. I started to cover the Kosovo area in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, please ask the witness to stop before answering a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're encouraged, Mr. Hutsch, to pause after the question, just for a few moments.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because the interpreters -- we're running in several languages and they're running in sequence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And they must catch up to the end of the question before you start the beginning of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did there come a time then in that period, in 1998, when you decided that you needed the use of an interpreter who could translate for you between the Albanian language and the German language?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I entered in 1998 first Macedonia, where I decided to -- to recruit an Albanian interpreter who speaks German and Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And were different candidates recommended to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes. In Germany there were seven candidates recommended by Albanian -- yeah, well-known people to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And did you -- did you then interview or speak with the different candidates?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yeah, I met all the seven candidates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Let me just -- I want to go slowly through this, all right. So when you met with these candidates, what criteria did you use to evaluate them in terms of whether they would be a competent and appropriate interpreter for you, or not?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: The first was they should possess a driving licence. The second was they should have a good knowledge of German language, and the third was I had a discussion with them to find out if they would give me KLA propaganda, in footsteps, Albanian propaganda or if they would have a neutral point of view on that what would go on in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. And based on your evaluations of the people who you interviewed, did you reject some of them?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yeah. I rejected five of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And why did you reject those five persons, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Out of my mind, three of them had been just a less knowledge of German language. And two of them, they speak fluently German, but in my eyes they were -- they did propaganda for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So they were not objective, in your mind?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you say you rejected five out of the seven persons. So does that mean you decided to hire two of the candidates?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes. Fortunately --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Let me -- and the two candidates that you hired, can you describe what their work and education -- work experience was at that time and their education level?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: The education level was that both had a university degree, made in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't quite understand. A degree in German or a degree that they had obtained in the country of Germany?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: They obtained in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay, all right. And you say that there were two. Both of these persons were going to work for you so that you could communicate with people who spoke Albanian. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And did there also come a time when you realised you needed an interpreter who could assist you in the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yeah. During the upcoming refugee crisis in spring 1999, when some refugee camps with Kosovo Albanian refugees rose up in -- in Macedonia, there was a need to -- yeah, to work together with Macedonian-speaking interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So did you repeat the process that you described before in order to hire a person who could translate for you between Macedonian and German?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes, I did the same way like I did with the Albanian interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how many interpreters did you hire who would speak the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: There were also two interpreters that I worked together with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did both of them speak German?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: No, just one was speaking German: The other one was speaking English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And again, in this process did you reject any of the applicants or did you hire just the first two people who came to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yeah. I rejected three up to five. I don't remember exactly, because there were some interviews just very short with these candidates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the two candidates that you selected, can you recall their educational levels or work experience?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: The first one did a university degree, and the second, a woman, she was working as a nurse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Can you explain, please -- let's -- now, this was -- this process occurred first in 1998, then in 1999. Obviously the situation in Macedonia became increasingly complicated going into 2001. Did there come a period when you returned to the Macedonia area?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yeah, I returned to Macedonia in 1999. I stayed there till October, November.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you use the same group of interpreters?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And how about after 1999?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: In 2000 I returned several times to Kosovo and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you use the same interpreters?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I was using the same interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And let's remember to try to pause between each of our sentences, all right, for the sake of the interpreters. Did there come a time in 2001 when you returned to Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes. In 2001, I returned in -- in January to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you began to -- and at that time you were working as a journalist?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were you working for a particular newspaper?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I was employed by the Hamburg Abendblatt. That is a daily in the north the Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And in 2001, did you use the same interpreters that you had hired in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. While you were working in Macedonia during 2001, can you describe, for example, how a typical workday for you, as a journalist, began?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: We started in the morning with a common breakfast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you, please. When you say "we started," who was "we"? Who was at this common breakfast?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: That depends on the mission that was planned for the day. Sometimes I just need the Macedonian speaking interpreter, sometimes I just need the Albanian speaking interpreter, and sometimes I need both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And, now, at this common breakfast, what would be discussed, what would be achieved?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: It was achieved first that we -- that the interpreters presented the -- the results of their -- I will say press view from the day before and what happened in the TV in the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In other words, if I could interrupt you, was it part of the job of your interpreters to also review what was coming out in the Macedonian media at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you continue, please. What would happen at the breakfast?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: We then discussed what was planned, what was the mission for today, what was our aim to find out in that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Who you're going to speak to in that --

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Who we are going to speak. Sometimes we --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we may, perhaps if Mr. Boskoski just could be asked to try to keep his voice down a little bit, because I'm hearing things here across the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is very difficult in a courtroom of this size, but I'm sure Mr. Boskoski will be conscious of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you continue, please. What would occur during the rest of this breakfast, these common breakfasts?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: So we discussed who we are going to speak with, what was the aim of the mission of this day, and, yeah, what was the purpose of what my newspaper would like to know about the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And when you then -- if you were, for example, to go with your interpreters then -- when you then began the day after breakfast with one or more interpreters, how would the communication be through the interpreters and the person you were speaking with?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: So that depends on the person. Sometimes we had sources who just would like to talk to the -- to the interpreter and there wasn't accept a foreigner in their discussion. So the interpreter has to do the interview with the guidelines we spoke about in the morning. Other -- other persons, they just would like to speak with me, and then the interpreter has to translate that what the other one spoke and that what I was asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Did you understand at this time in 2001 some words of Macedonian, some words of Albanian?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I understood a couple of words from both languages, just to -- to say hello and how are you to open on a low level talk and, yeah, that was my knowledge about both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And were there times when the interpreters interpreted words that you had already understood?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: I could see with this few words, if they translated in a right way or not, so that low level was the first control. But, on the other hand, I was doing some appointments together with another colleague, for example, and he brought his interpreter with him, so what we did is that we decided who of the interpreters would translate this discussion or this interview and so the other one was all the time a control element for the interpreter of the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So there was a way of checking the accuracy in those conversations?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How about at the end of a typical day. How would your day end after doing this work?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: The normal end was that we sit together with a beer or whatever, and we discussed the day and the results of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you for a moment. Again, just so that the record is clear, you used the pronoun "we." Who do you mean by "we"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: He was the interpreter I was together with in the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Sometimes more than one?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And what would you do during that discussion at the end of the day?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: We found out what we -- what we did in the day for which incidents we had two sources. That was always a basic rule of us that we just -- that we published just things we had two sources for. What we did is also that if there was something unclear to anybody in our team that we discussed this point to make it clear or to evaluate and we say we have to check that the next day or one of the following days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And by -- and if I can stop you there, by checking this point that might not have been clear to everyone, would that entail contacting the source again to clarify?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes. That would be part of this check.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever check your notes against either notes of interpreters or their memories?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yeah. We -- everybody did some notes in our team. And we checked these notes so that it was -- so that we were able to -- to fulfil the notes of the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: And in a moment where I have just been together with one of the interpreters, and they came aside where we had something like a political analyse, I checked myself with a phone call to the other interpreter if I just had something like propaganda from the other interpreter with the interpreter from the other ethnical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see, okay. And why did you feel it was important to do that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Because I think that a journalist, especially in a war area, has to be very objective. It's a part of his life insurance. So my experience in 12 years to be a war correspondent is if I'm objective and I'm neutral and I'm not doing propaganda, every side will protect me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Did that policy, if you will, also make it more likely that every side would speak with you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
